teaser.text: Equinix sells secure, powered places for other companies’ computers, plus the connections and operating help that make those computers useful. A dollar comes in through recurring space, power and connectivity charges, then goes out through electricity, people, buildings, expansion, equipment and financing before any remainder belongs to owners.

blocks.heading: Where could Equinix's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: Equinix’s weighted outcome reaches $1,085.28 in October 2027 and $1,249.45 in October 2029, including dividends, with returns hinging on power delivery, construction returns and financing.

The forecast assigns 24% probability to the bear case, 56% to the base case and 20% to the bull case. The weighted return is +11% by October 2027 and +32% by October 2029; the October 2029 scenarios span $728.27 to $1,848.65, with a $1,258.82 base case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Equinix?

paragraphs.text: The base case would gain support if revenue and AFFO-per-share growth track management’s targets, while MRR, bookings, and interconnections convert into recurring revenue. The bull case would become more credible if presold cabinets bill on schedule from late 2026 through 2027, repeat interconnection activity accelerates, and projects approach stabilized yields during 2028–2029.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Equinix really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow was approximately negative $1.46 billion over the twelve months through June 2026, equal to a negative 1.5% yield on the equity value. Existing centers can produce rent while new buildings consume cash before they are finished, leased and filled. Recurring capital expenditure is expected at roughly $290–310 million, against $4.71–5.69 billion of non-recurring expansion spending. Stock compensation adds a further issue: AFFO may add it back, but new shares spread future earnings across more owners.

blocks.heading: What does Equinix's stock price imply today?

paragraphs.text: The ordinary price-to-earnings ratio is approximately 64.1 times, but depreciation makes it a poor first measure for this REIT. Funds from operations, or FFO, adds back much of the depreciation charged against real estate. Adjusted funds from operations, or AFFO, goes further by subtracting recurring property spending. That makes AFFO closer to normalised cash earning power, although companies do not use one universal formula. Equinix trades at 33.4 times FFO and 24.1 times AFFO.

blocks.heading: Is Equinix's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.subsection: 5.7 — REIT structure, capital access and cash for shareholders
paragraphs.text: Equinix covers its dividend on AFFO, but its expansion program exceeds internally retained cash. A REIT owns or operates income-producing property and follows special tax and distribution rules; it generally must distribute 90% of taxable income to retain its tax status. That requirement concerns taxable income, not AFFO or all operating cash flow.

paragraphs.subsection: 5.7 — REIT structure, capital access and cash for shareholders
paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow was $3,911 million in 2025, but purchases of property, plant and equipment were $4,311 million. Dividends absorbed another $1,856 million, creating a funding gap before real-estate acquisitions of $994 million and other investing flows. This does not prove that the existing estate cannot fund upkeep. It shows that the expansion program is larger than internally retained cash.

paragraphs.text: The dividend grows more slowly than recent AFFO in the base case. It reaches $21.87 per share in the first window and $23.63 in the second. It reaches $25.52 by the final window. This uses 8% annual increases, below the latest 10% increase, because 2025 operating cash flow of $3,911 million was below property spending of $4,311 million.

The view would move toward the bear case if grid congestion delays commissioning during 2027–2028, or if sold-but-not-installed capacity accumulates through 2029. Higher refinancing costs, continued construction spending, and no buybacks would add pressure.

earnings.title: Equinix earnings: date, guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Equinix reports on October 28, 2026; management guides to $10,205–10,285 million of revenue and AFFO per diluted share of $42.69–43.29.
earnings.opening: Equinix reports its next results on October 28, 2026. Watch whether newly delivered capacity becomes recurring revenue.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Equinix’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Equinix guided for 2026 and 2027–2029?

paragraphs.text: Management guides to 2026 revenue of $10,205–10,285 million and AFFO per diluted share of $42.69–43.29. For 2027–2029, it targets revenue growth of 10.0–13.0% and AFFO-per-share growth of 9.0–12.0%, alongside annual capital expenditure of $5,000–7,000 million.

blocks.heading: Has Equinix kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management forecast AFFO per share of US$36.69–US$37.51 and delivered US$38.33. That deserves credit, but the central ownership question remains longer term: whether completed projects produce returns strong enough to overcome their financing, stock pay and dilution.

blocks.heading: What is Equinix’s trend over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Revenue and net operating income rose through 2025 even as occupancy fell from 82.0% in 2022 to 76.0% in 2025. AFFO per share climbed from $27.11 in 2021 to $38.33 in 2025. Diluted shares grew 2.4% in 2025, while the AFFO payout ratio was 49.0%; net debt to EBITDAre was 3.8x.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Equinix’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next decisive evidence is recurring revenue from newly delivered capacity. Equinix reports third-quarter results on October 28, 2026, when investors can compare recurring customer revenue with the July forecast and separate it from exceptional fees.
